dedupe_keys.name: who harmonized health facility assessment hhfa standard facility survey of service availability readiness and quality

description: This resource is the World Health Organization's Harmonized Health Facility Assessment, a standard survey that countries use to measure whether health facilities have the infrastructure, equipment, medicines, staff and management needed to provide services at required standards of quality. WHO and partners maintain it. It consists of modules with core and additional questions, a full and a quick implementation guide, questionnaires programmed in a CSPro electronic tool for tablets or phones, an indicator inventory with the code to calculate each indicator, downloadable as Excel, and OpenWHO training courses. Surveys are done by facility visits, through interviews, observation and records review, either on a representative sample of facilities or as a census of all facilities. Coverage is any country that implements it, and WHO is publishing HHFA and earlier SARA survey reports, with metadata and microdata to follow where countries authorise. The tools are free to download from WHO. Caveats: it is mainly a method and tool set, country surveys are periodic and not every report is released, and microdata access depends on each country. Simulation uses: a template for describing health facility capacity and service readiness in healthcare disruption and surge models, and a source of facility readiness indicators where surveys are published. Related records: DHIS2 (platform-dhis2) holds routine health data in many of the same countries, and the WHO Global Health Expenditure Database (data-who-global-health-expenditure-database) gives financing context.
